# An exact saturation-versus-positive-section alternative on a simplex base

This is an auxiliary geometric diagnostic for the positive-width active-cap problem. For \(n\geq2\), the base family below has at most \(n+2\leq2^n\) fibers and is already covered by the elementary heavy-fiber proof of OC. Its \(n=1\) three-fiber instance can lie outside that easy mass regime. No general OC payment follows from this note.

## 1. Setup

Let the complete integer base set consist of affinely independent vertices \(v_0,\ldots,v_n\) and one interior point
\[
p=\sum_{j=0}^n\alpha_jv_j,\qquad \alpha_j>0,\quad\sum_j\alpha_j=1.
\]
Assume all continuous fibers have positive \(d\)-volume, and
\[
K_p=\sum_j\alpha_jK_{v_j}. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(Y=(p,y)\), \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\), be an actual deepest source in the outward uniform-width model. The same statements hold with a fixed nonnegative through-source buffer \(b\).

Fix one ACTUAL active cap with normal \(N=(a,u)\), \(\Gamma(u)=1\), width \(h>0\). Put
\[
c_z=u\cdot y-a\cdot(z-p)-b,\qquad
E_z=K_z\cap\{c_z-h<u\cdot x<c_z\},
\]
and
\[
S_z=|E_z|/h.
\]
This is precisely the contribution of the \(z\)-fiber to the normal derivative coarea \(S\); it is not an auxiliary density.

## 2. The exact rank alternative

The base-normal stationarity equation gives
\[
\sum_jS_{v_j}(v_j-p)=0.
\]
The \(n\times(n+1)\) matrix with columns \(v_j-p\) has rank \(n\), and its nullspace is the span of \(\alpha\). Hence there is a scalar \(t\geq0\) such that
\[
S_{v_j}=t\alpha_j\quad\text{for every }j. \tag{2}
\]
Thus either every outside strip contribution vanishes, or every outside vertex fiber contributes positive strip volume. There is no intermediate rank-deficient positive pattern.

If \(t=0\), convexity and positive fiber dimension force the smooth capture on each outside fiber to be identically zero or identically one: a continuous affine functional whose range intersects the open transition interval would give it positive volume. All outside fibers cannot be missed. Indeed that would imply
\[
h_{K_{v_j}}(u)\leq c_{v_j}-h
\]
for every \(j\). Taking their \(\alpha\)-average and using (1) and \(\sum\alpha_jc_{v_j}=c_p=u\cdot y-b\) gives
\[
h_{K_p}(u)\leq u\cdot y-b-h,
\]
contradicting \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\).

Let \(V_{\min}=\min_j|K_{v_j}|\). Therefore the outside captured mass in this zero-strip case is at least \(V_{\min}\). Conversely a generic pure-base direction can capture exactly ANY chosen vertex and miss all other vertices, because \(p\) is strictly interior to their simplex. Scaling it by a sufficiently large finite factor saturates that sign pattern while preserving the own-fiber cap. Choosing a cheapest vertex gives an actual competing cap with the same own-fiber contribution and outside contribution exactly \(V_{\min}\).

Actual cap minimality forces equality. Consequently the original cap captures exactly one cheapest outside vertex fiber, and its outside saturation deficit is zero. Its continuous normal can be retargeted to any fixed cheapest vertex, preserving the actual active mass.

A balanced menu entirely of this type therefore has a favorable common target and pays. A SINGLE retargetable cap does not imply that the whole needed continuous balance can be supported on such caps.

In the notation of the saturation-deficit note, any active cap with \(\Delta_N>0\) must satisfy \(t>0\), and thus must have a positive transition strip on EVERY outside vertex fiber.

## 3. An actual strip-volume constraint in the positive branch

The strip thresholds obey \(\sum_j\alpha_jc_{v_j}=c_p\). Therefore (1) gives the genuine set inclusion
\[
\sum_j\alpha_jE_{v_j}\subset E_p.
\]
Ordinary \(d\)-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski, followed by (2), yields
\[
(hS_p)^{1/d}\geq\sum_j\alpha_j(hS_{v_j})^{1/d},
\]
hence
\[
S_p\geq t\left(\sum_j\alpha_j^{\,1+1/d}\right)^d. \tag{3}
\]
For equal barycentric weights on \(m=n+1\) vertices, this says \(S_p\geq t/m\), so the own strip contributes at least the fraction \(1/(m+1)\) of the total strip mass \(S_p+t\).

The open strips are convex bodies up to their measure-zero boundaries when their volumes are positive. Brunn--Minkowski can equivalently be applied to their compact closures, which changes none of the volumes. The common strip width and normal normalization are unchanged across fibers.

If a zero-width limit has proper sections at every outside fiber, the analogous Minkowski inclusion in the common \((d-1)\)-dimensional section planes gives (3) with exponent \(d-1\) for \(d\geq2\). This last assertion requires that actual proper-section limits exist; it does not replace supporting-incidence selectors or assume that a mixed intrinsic limit is uniform.

## 4. Exact scope

The dichotomy uses the simplex-base linear dependence and the actual Minkowski equality (1). For a general finite base set, nonnegative strip masses can have more complicated support, so (2) need not hold. If the middle fiber strictly contains the Minkowski average, all outside fibers may be missed by a cap cutting a protruding part of the middle fiber; the above exclusion then fails.

Equation (3) is a kernel-mass lower bound. It is not a lower bound on captured cap mass, on physical boundary credit, or on the continuous Grünbaum fraction. A quantitative payment of the all-positive branch remains separate.
